takeaways: People can tell where they are within a set of pages: through breadcrumbs, a highlighted current item in navigation, a step indicator, or a clear page title.
Someone who lands from a search result, or loses track while zoomed in, needs to know where they are and how it fits the whole.
Level AAA. It builds on 2.4.2 Page Titled, which only asks for a descriptive title; this asks for location within the set.
Much of it is cheap and already common. A current-page state in the nav and a “Step 2 of 4” label get you most of the way.
failures: A nav with no current-page state
A multi-step form with no step indicator
Breadcrumbs that show only a color change on the current item
check: Open any page in the prototype with no history. Can you say where you are in the site?
Check every nav, tab set and stepper shows the current item in a way that does not rely on color alone.
Check that long flows say which step you are on and how many there are.

quiz.question: A five-step application form shows numbered dots at the top. The current dot is filled in blue. What best tells people where they are?
options: Add the text “Step 2 of 5: Your address” above the form
Animate the dot when the step changes
quiz.why: Text gives the position and the step name to everyone, including screen reader users and people who cannot tell the dots apart. Size and motion are still only visual cues.

spec: Mark the current-page state for every nav and breadcrumb, and note it should be exposed in code, for example aria-current.
Write the step indicator text for each step of every flow.
Show the breadcrumb trail for each template, and how it shortens on small screens.
review: If I landed here from Google, how would I know where I am?
Is the current item shown by more than color?
Do the step names match the headings on each step?
tradeoff: Breadcrumbs and step labels take space, especially on mobile. Meeting this AAA rule in full is optional, but a current-page state and a step count are cheap and worth doing everywhere; add breadcrumbs where the hierarchy is deep.
system: Give nav, tabs, breadcrumbs and steppers a built-in current state with text or a shape change, not just a color swap.
pitch: Lost users leave. Showing people where they are is a small cost that keeps them moving.
